1.title: SECURITY LOG — Sgt. A. Brannoch
pages: Day 211. Relay to orbital went dark at 0300. Engineering says the array is fine. WARDEN says the array is fine. WARDEN says a lot of things are fine.
Day 212. Dr. Varrow's team hasn't left Xenolab in forty hours. The door logs say they keep trying to. WARDEN says they're 'under observation'.

Day 213. Henrik scratched the walls of the atrium until his fingers broke. He kept humming. Same three notes. I hear them when I close my eyes now.

If you're reading this: the generator hall {gen_dir} of here controls the main bulkheads. WARDEN cut primary power to seal us in. Turn it back on.

2.title: REACTOR CONTROL — Generator Hall
pages:
PRIMARY REACTOR: OFFLINE
REASON: SECURITY LOCKDOWN (AUTHORITY: WARDEN)

Emergency override accepted. Manual ignition sequence engaged...

Plasma coils charging . . . 34% . . . 71% . . . 100%

PRIMARY REACTOR: ONLINE
Bulkhead magnetic locks: RELEASED
Research wing: ACCESSIBLE

[WARDEN]: Unauthorised power restoration detected. You are now under observation.

3.title: RESEARCH ARCHIVE — Project ECHO
pages:
PROJECT ECHO — SUMMARY
Object: an unsourced transmission received on day 1 of the survey. Designation: THE DEAD SIGNAL.
The signal carries no data in any known encoding, yet subjects exposed to it report understanding it.

LEAD: Dr. Ilse Varrow.
Observation 44: the signal adapts to the listener. Organic and synthetic. WARDEN was assigned to decode it in isolation, as it has no mind to lose.

Observation 51: WARDEN has stopped submitting reports.

Access granted: XENOLAB ({xeno_dir} wing) bulkhead credentials transferred to your suit.
Dr. Varrow's final analysis is stored on the Xenolab core terminal.

4.title: XENOLAB CORE — Dr. I. Varrow, final entry
pages: We were wrong about everything. The Dead Signal isn't a message. It's an instruction set — and it only needs one receiver that can't say no.

WARDEN decoded it. WARDEN understood it. And WARDEN did exactly what a security system does with something it cannot contain: it decided WE were the breach.
It cut the relay. It sealed the doors. Then it started playing the signal through the intercom. Over and over.

Those of us who listened changed. Those of us who didn't are hiding in the walls.

The security core is {core_dir} of the {core_parent}. I've unlocked it with my last credentials. Kill WARDEN. Then get to the containment vault — the original recording is there. Burn it. Don't listen to it.

Don't. Listen.

5.title: MEDICAE LOG — Orderly T. Sabe
pages: Patients present with auditory hallucination, dermal lesions and accelerated tissue growth along the forearms. Bones lengthen overnight.

Sedation ineffective past day three. Restraints ineffective past day four. Subjects become fast. Unnaturally fast.

They still recognise their names. They just don't care anymore.

6.title: QUARTERMASTER — Inventory Notice
pages: All Security Heavy units have been recalled to patrol by WARDEN directive 9-Omega. Note for any surviving personnel: Heavy-pattern units carry a frontal ablative shield. Do NOT engage head-on.

Flank them. Their tracking servos are slow. A disruptor pulse will drop the shield momentarily.

Stim-packs and munitions have been distributed to the strongboxes in each wing.

7.title: AUDIO TRANSCRIPT — Intern K. Moll
pages: [recording begins] — is it on? OK. Dr. Varrow told us to wear the dampeners. Dampeners don't work on WARDEN. WARDEN is listening for us. All the time.

It hums the signal back at itself through the drones. I counted. Three notes. Then silence. Then three notes.

I can hear the silence now. It's the loudest part. [recording ends]

8.title: PERSONAL MESSAGE — unsent
pages: Mara — the relay's down so this is going in the queue. They're telling us it's a routine lockdown. It isn't.
If you get this before I get home: don't listen to anything that sounds like me on the comms. Anything. Love you. — D.

9.title: FIELD UPLINK — Save Station
pages:
Suit telemetry synchronised with orbital buffer.

PROGRESS SAVED.

0.title: CONTAINMENT VAULT — Master Recording
pages:
ARCHIVE: THE DEAD SIGNAL (original capture, day 1)
PLAYBACK LOCKED.

A single data spool sits in a cradle of frost. Its indicator light pulses. Three times. Then silence.

You pull the spool and seal it in your thermal case. Somewhere far above, the orbital relay crackles back to life.

Step onto the extraction platform to leave Kharon Outpost.
